title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named Harding University spaces for studying, meeting, recreation, art, performances and campus connection, verified through current university sources.

cards.title: Book a Room or Build a Project
cards.subtitle: Study rooms, workstations and project support
cards.notes: Use a small study room for group work, then visit the Media Center or Writing Center when the assignment needs another kind of help.
cards.short_summary: A study base with rooms, computers, printing and hands-on academic support in one building.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding states that Brackett Library serves students with conference and small study rooms, more than 60 public workstations, printers, a Writing Center and a Media Center.
cards.source_title: Brackett Library | Catalog, Archives & Research | Harding
cards.access_notes: Library access and individual services follow their posted operating schedules and applicable student-use procedures.

cards.title: Meet Around the Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: A practical hub for errands and conversation
cards.notes: Use the lounge as a meeting point, then handle mail, bookstore, market or Student Life errands without crossing campus again.
cards.short_summary: The student center combines a social lounge with several everyday campus services.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding’s undergraduate handbook identifies Hammon Student Center as its campus hub and documents a student lounge for meeting friends alongside mail, bookstore, market and student-service offices.
cards.access_notes: Campus services and food outlets inside the building maintain their own schedules and eligibility requirements.

cards.title: Rotate Through Indoor Recreation
cards.subtitle: Pool, courts, track and student fitness spaces
cards.notes: Check the current GAC schedule in Pipeline before choosing among the pool, elevated track, courts, weight room or exercise areas.
cards.short_summary: A single indoor facility supports multiple forms of student recreation and exercise.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding lists basketball, volleyball, swimming, pickleball, racquetball, badminton, billiards, table tennis, a weight room, an aerobics room and an elevated track at the GAC.
cards.source_title: Kinesiology Facilities | Labs, Gyms and Research | Harding
cards.access_notes: The official page directs users to Pipeline for the GAC schedule; accommodations and facility requirements may apply.

cards.title: Take Recreation Outdoors
cards.subtitle: Lighted courts, fields, trail and disc golf
cards.notes: Choose a lighted court or field for a group game, or use the jogging trail and disc-golf course for a self-paced outing.
cards.short_summary: Bison Lane gathers several outdoor recreation choices into one named campus area.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding documents lighted tennis, sand volleyball, outdoor basketball, lighted flag-football and soccer fields, a multipurpose field, an 18-hole disc-golf course and a jogging trail at Bison Lane.
cards.source_title: Kinesiology Facilities | Labs, Gyms and Research | Harding
cards.access_notes: Outdoor facility availability can depend on daylight, weather, scheduled programs and current recreation rules.

cards.title: Move a Study Session Outside
cards.subtitle: The historic lawn at the center of campus
cards.notes: Bring portable coursework for an outdoor study session, while keeping paths open and checking conditions before settling in.
cards.short_summary: Harding explicitly presents the Front Lawn as a place for students to study outdoors.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding’s student-life page describes students studying on the Front Lawn, while its history tour identifies the lawn as a named historic campus location.
cards.source_title: Student at Harding | Spiritual Life, Clubs and Dorms | Harding
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor campus lawn; use depends on weather, grounds conditions and any scheduled university activity.

cards.title: Pause Between Classes for an Exhibition
cards.subtitle: Student, faculty and visiting work on display
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition, then spend a few minutes looking closely; senior shows and portfolio reviews add student work to the mix.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery where student projects and visiting exhibitions share the same walls.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding says Stevens Art Gallery hosts student showcases, senior shows, sophomore portfolio reviews, collaborative branding shows and exhibitions by visiting artists.
cards.access_notes: The official page lists Monday-Friday access from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.; exhibitions follow the academic calendar.

cards.title: See the Student Body Take the Stage
cards.subtitle: Chapel, theatre and large campus productions
cards.notes: Consult the event calendar before going; the room shifts from regular chapel gatherings to student-heavy theatrical productions.
cards.short_summary: Harding’s large auditorium is shared across recurring gatherings and major student performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding’s current theatre schedule places the Homecoming musical and Spring Sing in Benson Auditorium and describes Spring Sing as showcasing more than 1,000 students.
cards.source_title: Theatre Events and Productions | Harding University
cards.access_notes: Admission and access vary by event; performances may require tickets, while other university gatherings follow separate rules.

cards.entity_name: Reynolds Center for Music and Communication
cards.title: Practice Beyond the Classroom
cards.subtitle: Rehearsal halls, classrooms and piano rooms
cards.notes: Music students can use the building’s practice-room resources between rehearsals; confirm room procedures with the department first.
cards.short_summary: The music building supports individual practice as well as shared rehearsal and classroom work.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding states that the Reynolds Center includes rehearsal halls, classrooms and practice rooms equipped with electronic, upright and grand pianos.
cards.source_title: Undergraduate Majors in Music and Music Education | Harding
cards.access_notes: Practice rooms are departmental facilities; availability and eligibility should be confirmed with the Music Department.

cards.title: Connect With International Programs
cards.subtitle: Study-abroad and international-student services
cards.notes: Start here when comparing study-abroad programs or looking for international-student support, then confirm appointments with the relevant office.
cards.short_summary: A shared academic home for international programs, languages, history, political science and ROTC.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding says Holland-Waller Center houses the Swaid Institute for International Education, including study-abroad programs and international-student services, plus several academic departments.
cards.access_notes: Public circulation and office appointments may differ; contact the applicable program before seeking staff assistance.

cards.title: Follow the Garden Path Behind Pattie Cobb
cards.subtitle: An outdoor classroom and connected gardens
cards.notes: Walk behind Pattie Cobb Hall to explore the garden areas and outdoor classroom, respecting any class or scheduled gathering underway.
cards.short_summary: A named garden complex offering a quieter outdoor setting beside central campus buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Harding’s 2026 Homecoming page directs visitors to the First Ladies Garden, outdoor classroom, secret garden and serendipity garden behind Pattie Cobb Hall near Shores and Pryor halls.
cards.access_notes: The gardens are outdoors; access depends on weather, grounds conditions and any classes or university events using the area.
